jobs.occupation: PhD fellowship on Street-level Bureaucracy of Regulatory Implementation for AI
jobs.description:
The Human Centered Computing Section at the Department of Computer Science, Faculty of Science at the University of Copenhagen invites applicants for a PhD fellowship on Street-level Bureaucracy of Regulatory Implementation for AI.

  The start date is expected to be 1 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.
  

  The position

  This doctoral position is part of REGULAIRE (Regulatory Learning for the Governance of Transformative Technologies) is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network bringing together 15 doctoral candidates at ten European universities to study how regulation can learn and adapt in situations where technologies, risks, and expectations change quickly. Its projects examine how regulators sense emerging problems early, how balanced interventions encourage learning without overcorrection or underreaction, how such interventions alter institutional capacities, and how feedback can be institutionalised so that insights travel across organisations and jurisdictions.

   

  Project description

  The PhD student’s research is expected to conduct in-depth qualitative studies of how EU digital regulation (e.g., AIA, DSA) is technically and organisationally implemented in SMEs developing AI-related technologies. The goal is to map developers’ translation of regulatory guidance into product and service design and compares implementation strategies across sectors. This project offers a focused route into human-centred computing, sociotechnical research and the study of regulation in practice. You will join an international cohort, receive supervision across institutions and take part in three residential summer schools, methods workshops, monthly paper development seminars and joint work with regulators, standardisation bodies and international organisations. Every project includes a planned three-month intersectoral secondment.

  The PhD student to be recruited in this call is expected to define their PhD project within the scope of the overall project and collaborate with the larger project team.

   

  Description of the scientific environment

  The position will be within the Human Centered Computing section (HCC). The Human Centered Computing section is a highly interdisciplinary group that conducts research within the areas of Human-Computer Interaction, Computer Supported Cooperative Work, Ubiquitous and Pervasive Computing, Digital Fabrication and related fields. Our section aspires to be a top research environment that bridges technology, theory, and empirical studies. The Human Centered Computing research environment at the University of Copenhagen is internationally leading, as evidenced by it’s ranking as second in Europe according to CSRankings. Further information about research at the Department is available here: https://di.ku.dk/english/research/ .

  This position will be co-supervised by Irina Shklovski (email: ias@di.ku.dk) and Naja Holten Møller (email: naja@di.ku.dk) at the University of Copenhagen in the Department of Computer Science, Human-Centered Computing section. The PhD will be conducted in collaboration with Joris Van Hoboken, Professor of Information Law, with special emphasis on Law and Digital Infrastructure at the Institute for Information Law (IViR), Faculty of Law, University of Amsterdam

   

  Who are we looking for?

   	
• Applicants should hold a MSc degree or equivalent in Computer Science, Data Science, HCI, Critical Data Studies, STS, Law and Policy or a related field. 	
• Good written and oral English skills are a requirement. 	
• Previous scientific publications (if any) and relevant work experience is encouraged 	
• Applicants must be willing to engage in international mobility, including the planned secondment and network-wide activities   The ideal candidate would have an educational background or prior work experience in technology development, prior experience in qualitative research and fieldwork in organisations, and some understanding of European regulatory and policy concerns around AI systems.
  

  The PhD programme

  You can undertake the PhD programme as:

  A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish Master’s degree.

  Getting into a position on the regular PhD programme 

  Qualifications needed for the regular programme
 To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme equivalent to a Danish Master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the position, i.e. HCI or CS. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Additional qualifications for the MSCA PhD 

  REGULAIRE is funded by the European Commission’s Marie Skłodowska-Curie programme and to be eligible for this funding you must meet the following criteria:

   	
• You must not have resided or carried out your main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Denmark for more than 12 months in the 3 years immediately prior to your recruitment; 	
• You must work on the project full-time.   Please ensure that this information is clear on your CV. Researchers can be of any nationality.

   

  Terms of employment in the regular programme 
 Employment as a PhD fellow is full time, on site in Copenhagen, and for maximum 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific position formulated by the applicant.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

   

  Responsibilities and tasks in the PhD programme

   	
• Carry out a research project with increasing autonomy from your supervisors 	
• Collaborate with researchers both within the research group, and with external project partners 	
• Author scientific papers aimed at high-impact venues 	
• Participate in the research and training activities with the REGULAIRE network 	
• Disseminate research nationally and internationally 	
• Attend PhD courses on general skills development such as academic writing, as well as relevant specialised courses such as REGULAIRE summer and winter schools 	
• Conduct a change of scientific environment in the form of a secondment with a relevant standards organisation and an extended visit with one of the REGULAIRE academic partners 	
• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project    

  We are looking for the following qualifications:

   	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD position 	
• Relevant educational background 	
• Relevant publications 	
• Relevant work experience 	
• Other relevant professional activities 	
• Good written and oral English language skills    

  Application and Assessment Procedure

  Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include: 

   	
• Cover Letter detailing your motivation and background for applying for this PhD position; 	
• Research Statement detailing your desired research focus and goals for the PhD studies within the scope of the specified position. The research statement should demonstrate your independent thinking by outlining a concrete research direction within technology governance you wish to explore, including: specific research questions you aim to address, preliminary ideas on methodological approaches you would employ, connections to existing literature, and the potential impact and applications; 	
• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position; 	
• Original diplomas for Bachelor’s and Master’s degrees and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted; 	
• Publication list (if available); 	
• Names and contact details of three references.    

  Application deadline: 

  The deadline for applications is November 22, 23:59 GMT +1. 

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After the deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by unbiased expert assessors. You will be notified about whether your application will be selected for assessment.

  The assessors will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above-mentioned research area, skills and other requirements. The assessors will conclude whether each applicant is qualified. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessments. You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

  Interviews with selected candidates are expected to be held in December

   

  Questions

  For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact ias@di.ku.dk  

  General information about PhD study at the Faculty of SCIENCE is available at the PhD School’s website: https://www.science.ku.dk/phd/.

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position.

**Job Description

**Do you want to define the evaluation methodology and technical requirements that underpin effective AI evaluation and monitoring within the business at one of the leading financial institutions in the Nordics?

Join Danske Bank's newly established AI Model Assessment team in Business Controls & Product Management. As AI Evaluation Methodology & Platform Requirements Lead, you will hold a 1st Line of Defence role with clear ownership of the technical methodologies used to evaluate AI models and AI-enabled solutions, and of the technical requirements for the platforms that support their evaluation and ongoing monitoring. You will translate business-owned risk and control needs into clear methods, metrics, data, evidence, traceability and platform capabilities that can be implemented consistently across the Bank's technology landscape.

This is a unique opportunity to shape a consistent, scalable and evidence-based capability through which the business identifies, evaluates, monitors and manages AI model risk.

This role can be based in Copenhagen, Denmark, Vilnius, Lithuania, Warsaw, Poland, Stockholm, Sweden or Helsinki, Finland.

**What You Will Be Doing

**The AI Model Assessment team is a business-owned control capability that performs evidence-based assessments of AI models and AI-enabled solutions across the Bank. We work with business owners, developers, engineers and platform teams to understand how solutions operate, define the evidence required for assessment, and establish the evaluation and monitoring capabilities needed to identify, assess and manage model risk where it arises.

Our mission is to enable responsible innovation by providing the business with a consistent and scalable framework for evaluating AI systems, monitoring their performance and risk, and demonstrating that appropriate controls are operating effectively.

As AI Evaluation Methodology & Platform Requirements Lead, you will own the evaluation methodology and define the technical requirements for the platforms, tooling and data capabilities used by the 1st Line of Defence to evaluate and monitor AI models and AI-enabled solutions. Your mandate is to ensure that the business has robust, implementable and auditable means to assess its AI risks and controls. Your focus will be on specifying what the evaluation and monitoring capability must deliver rather than owning software development or platform operations.

You will work closely with the independent 2nd Line AI model risk function, which sets the overarching risk framework and provides oversight and constructive challenge. You will translate that framework into practical evaluation methodologies, technical requirements and business-owned controls, provide transparent evidence of how requirements are implemented, and support the resolution of identified gaps.

**Your responsibilities will include:

**

• Owning, developing and maintaining the methodology for evaluating AI models and AI-enabled solutions, including evaluation objectives, test approaches, acceptance criteria and evidence standards.

• Defining the functional and technical requirements for evaluation and monitoring platforms that enable risk management, including data ingestion, test execution, metric calculation, observability, evidence capture, reporting, access controls and auditability.

• Translating model risk, business and assessment requirements into reusable evaluation methods, representative datasets, metrics, thresholds, monitoring indicators and structured evidence requirements.

• Determining how AI system architectures, components, dependencies and data flows affect evaluation scope, test design, monitoring coverage and the technical capabilities required from supporting platforms.

• Defining platform-agnostic requirements that support evaluation and monitoring across environments such as AWS Bedrock and AgentCore, Databricks, Azure OpenAI and embedded third-party AI platforms.

• Setting requirements for reproducibility and end-to-end traceability across models, prompts, datasets, configurations, system components, evaluation results, monitoring signals and changes over time.

• Prioritising opportunities to standardise and automate evaluation and monitoring activities, and working with evaluators, platform owners and engineers to convert approved control requirements into practical platform capabilities.

• Engaging with the Second Line model risk function to interpret applicable requirements, demonstrate how they are operationalised, respond to constructive challenge, and ensure that evaluation and monitoring evidence supports effective independent oversight.

**About You

**An experienced AI evaluation, model risk, data, architecture or platform professional who can establish rigorous evaluation methodologies and turn business risk and control needs into clear, implementable technical requirements for enterprise platforms and tooling.

You have:

• Proven experience designing or governing AI/ML evaluation methodologies, including test objectives, datasets, metrics, thresholds, acceptance criteria and evidence standards.

• Experience translating evaluation, monitoring, risk and control needs into functional and technical requirements for platforms, tooling, data pipelines and reporting capabilities.

• Experience with AI/ML evaluation, business-owned model risk management and controls, technical assurance, MLOps, LLMOps, AI platforms or AI observability.

• Familiarity with cloud AI services or enterprise AI platforms; experience with AWS Bedrock or AgentCore, Databricks or Mosaic AI, Azure OpenAI, or comparable platforms is an advantage.

• Strong understanding of evaluation and monitoring principles, including representative datasets, experiment configuration, metric design, regression testing, monitoring indicators, traceability and evidence capture.

• Ability to distinguish methodology and requirements ownership from platform implementation, while collaborating effectively with engineers and platform owners. Python or similar tools for analysis, prototyping or investigation are an advantage, but software development is not the primary focus of the role.

• Excellent collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to articulate evaluation, monitoring, risk and control requirements across business, assessment, platform, engineering, architecture, data and risk functions.

Experience with AI evaluation or observability technologies, for example Phoenix or comparable tools, is an advantage but is not a prerequisite.

**What We Offer You

**You will join the newly established AI Model Assessment team in Business Controls & Product Management, helping build the Bank's consistent and scalable business-owned capability for AI evaluation, monitoring and model risk management.

The team combines technical AI evaluation expertise with model risk management and works across the Bank's AI initiatives. In this role, you will connect evaluators with platform, engineering, architecture and data teams by defining the methods and technical requirements their solutions must support, ensuring that risk ownership and control evidence remain anchored in the business.

If hired in Lithuania, your monthly salary would range from 4320 EUR to 6480 EUR gross (based on your competencies relevant for the job).

Additionally, each Danske Bank employee receives employee benefits package which includes:

• Growth opportunities: professional & supportive team, e-learnings, numerous development programs; (incl. professional certificates); 100+ professions for internal mobility opportunities.

• Health & Well-being: a diverse, inclusive, work & life balance work environment; additional health insurance; mental well-being practices; partial psychologist counselling compensation; silence and sleep zones at the office; game rooms.

• Hybrid working conditions: Work from home up to two days a week; home office budget (after the probation period); modern Danske Campus workplace developed with anthropologist for the best employee experience.

• Additional days of leave: for rest, health, volunteering, exams in higher education institutions, and other important activities. Moreover, for seniority with Danske Bank.

• Monetary compensation package: accidents & critical diseases insurance; financial support in case of unfortunate events, travel insurance; IIIrd Pillar Pension Fund contribution.

See all the benefits HERE**.

**Your job function (position) in the job contract will be AI Science

**Are you ready for the next step?

**If you are passionate about defining robust AI evaluation methodologies and the technical requirements for scalable evaluation and monitoring platforms that support effective business ownership of AI risk, we would love to hear from you.

For questions about the role, please contact Khaled Alizai, Head of AI Model Assessment at khali@danskebank.dk. We are screening the applications on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply.

Join us and help build the business-owned foundation for effective AI model evaluation, monitoring and risk management at Danske Bank.

Are you ready to take the next step into leadership while staying close to operations in a global logistics setup? We are looking for a Team Leader for Customer Care (Overseas) to lead a team of skilled Logistics Coordinators handling global order-to-delivery processes. This is a unique opportunity to combine people leadership with hands-on operational responsibility in a fast-paced, highly collaborative environment.

“You will take on a key role leading a skilled Customer Care team, balancing daily operations with people development while collaborating across the business to deliver excellent service to our global customers,” says Hiring Manager, Lasse Tarnok Larsen.

**How You Will Make An Impact

**This role is part of Customer Care within the Commercial business area, where you will lead a team of Logistic Coordinators responsible for managing order-to-delivery processes and customer communication for overseas markets.

You will balance operational execution with people leadership, ensuring high service quality while developing your team and driving continuous improvements. You will play a key role in coordinating across Sales, Supply Chain, Finance, and external partners to deliver strong customer outcomes.

Your main responsibility will include

• Leading, coach, and develop a team of Logistics Coordinators, ensuring engagement and performance

• Managing and prioritizing daily operations, including handling escalations and complex customer cases

• Coordinate with internal stakeholders and external logistics partners to ensure timely and efficient deliveries

• Drive continuous improvements in processes, data quality, and ways of working

• Take an active role in daily operations through responsibility of selected customers

**What Will Make You Successful

**To succeed in this role, you combine a strong operational foundation with the motivation to grow as a leader in a complex and fast-paced environment. You have hands-on experience within international logistics, particularly sea freight and air freight operations, supply chain, or customer service, and you understand the dynamics of global order-to-delivery processes and cross-functional collaboration. You are comfortable working with multiple stakeholders and know how to balance operational priorities with long-term improvements. Ideally, you bring a few years of relevant experience and are ready to take the next step in your leadership journey.

We hope that you will bring

• Experience within international logistics, particularly sea freight and air freight operations supply chain, or customer service, ideally linked to order-to-delivery processes

• Solid stakeholder management skills and the ability to collaborate across functions

• A clear and engaging leadership approach that builds trust and develops others

• Strong prioritisation and decision-making skills in a fast-paced environment

• A collaborative and relationship-driven mindset, working effectively with both internal and external stakeholders

At the same time, your personal approach is what will truly make a difference. You build trust through your ability to engage and support others, while also providing clear direction when needed. You thrive in an environment where priorities can shift quickly and where decisions need to be made with both speed and sound judgement. As a leader, you are motivated by developing people and creating a positive team culture, while ensuring high standards in delivery and collaboration.

**What do we offer?

**This is a unique opportunity to step into a leadership role with real responsibility and impact. You will join a collaborative and international environment where you can grow both professionally and personally.

We offer

• A strong entry point into leadership with coaching and development opportunities

• Exposure to global logistics and cross-functional collaboration

• A culture built on trust, empowerment, and teamwork

• Opportunities to develop your leadership career within Arla

Looking for a role where you can safeguard and steer a growing portfolio of non-recourse financings after financial close? Join our Project and Asset Finance team in Copenhagen as a Portfolio Management Professional and help manage EE's financing obligations across Europe.

European Energy is a growing company in the renewable energy sector. We are a privately owned Danish company founded in 2004, with our headquarters in Copenhagen. We develop, construct, finance, and operate solar (PV) and wind energy projects globally, as well as Power-to-X projects. In addition, we explore new technologies, including battery storage, biogas, and carbon capture. Our core values form the foundation of everything we do: In It Together, Trust and Courage, Ambition, Excitement, Inclusion, and Agility.

Your New Team

As a part of the CCO Area, the Project and Asset Finance team is responsible for sourcing all financing needed to construct EE's project pipeline, and for managing that financing through construction and operation.

In this role, you will work directly with the Global Head of Project and Asset Finance, the transaction deal teams, Asset Management, and Treasury, as well as the more than 25 other members of the broader M&A and Project Finance department dedicated to commercialising EE's asset portfolio.

Your New Role

As our new Portfolio Management Professional, you will, in collaboration with colleagues within our Asset Management and Treasury departments, take ownership of EE's financing obligations once a transaction reaches financial close. You will track asset finance transactions through construction and operation, quality-assure disbursements, reporting, waivers, and amendments, and act as the link between the deal team, Asset Management, and Treasury. This is a role for someone who wants broad visibility across a growing portfolio of non-recourse financings and a direct hand in keeping it in good order.

Your Responsibilities

• Assist with transaction closing and documentation ahead of financial close.

• Ensure a timely, clear, and detailed handoff of post-closing responsibilities to other internal stakeholders.

• Shadow and track all transactions throughout construction, providing support and quality assurance on disbursements, construction reporting, waivers, and amendments.

• Support and quality-assure the work of Asset Management during material restructurings

• and amendments.

• Quality-assure the payment of scheduled principal and interest to lenders.

• Track all asset finance transactions booked across the portfolio.

• Coordinate with Treasury to provide timely and accurate information on portfolio exposures.

• Manage all relationships with lender portfolio management counterparties.

• Support in periodic and ah-hoc reporting of portfolio obligations and status.

• Collaborate with M&A colleagues on common reporting obligations.

Prerequisites to progress in the job

• You have a minimum of 4 years of relevant experience in project finance, loan or portfolio administration, agency, or credit/portfolio monitoring roles, ideally within renewable energy or infrastructure.

• You have experience with post-closing management of non-recourse financings, including disbursements, covenant compliance, and reporting obligations.

• You have exposure to restructurings, workouts, or amendments, and are comfortable in quality-assuring the work of others.

• You have strong attention to detail and can work confidently across a large, growing portfolio of transactions.

• You have solid financial modelling and analytical skills, and a robust understanding of financing documentation.

As a person, you are structured and detail-oriented and can be trusted to keep track of many transactions in parallel without losing sight of what matters. You are a natural coordinator, comfortable working across the deal team, Asset Management, and Treasury, and you communicate clearly with both technical and financial audiences. You have a genuine interest in the financial market and the renewable energy sector.

You may be asked to travel occasionally to meet with stakeholders across Europe.

With us you get

• Close collaboration with senior colleagues and meaningful deal ownership from day one

• A culture of knowledge sharing and international collaboration across 21+ countries

• Flexible work policy and a diverse, inclusive work environment

• Opportunities for career advancement in a growing company and sector

• Six weeks of paid annual leave, a subsidised lunch scheme, employee discounts on glasses, furniture, and massage, free access to a gym, a mobile phone for both professional and personal use, and access to professional development opportunities, including on-the-job learning, internal and external training, and networking.

European Energy at a glance — The Power of Tomorrow, Today

We are now more than 970 employees with 51 nationalities represented in 21 countries, and we are growing rapidly in both Copenhagen and across our global offices. We all work for our common goal: to be a leading partner in the renewable energy transition and to create The Power of Tomorrow, Today.

Our working environment is built on mutual respect for the varied strengths and talents of our employees, with a flat hierarchy and a culture that encourages initiative and innovation. Our employees value our flexible working culture, which supports a better balance between work and personal life. We are a team, whether it is in the workplace, on our company trips, or during our weekly company training sessions. At European Energy, you will work with colleagues from around the world and become part of a collaborative international network.

We lead with purpose

At European Energy, our leadership culture is built on six guiding principles that shape how we collaborate, make decisions, and grow together. These principles help us act responsibly and empower each other to succeed.

Apply now

Workplace: Søborg, Denmark

Reference: Jeremy Bennett, Director, Global Head of Project and Asset Finance

To support a fair and unbiased recruitment process, we kindly ask that you do not include a photograph in your CV. We assess all candidates based on their skills, experience, qualifications, and potential to succeed in the role. We review applications and conduct interviews on an ongoing basis and will close the position once a suitable candidate has been identified. We therefore encourage you to apply as soon as possible. Please note that we do not accept applications via email or any other direct messaging channels. Applications must be submitted through the designated application link.

Contact person: For more information about the position, please reach out to Jeremy Bennett, jben@europeanenergy.com

**At Paychex Europe, we simplify payroll, HR and workforce management for businesses across Europe. We believe great results come from people who take ownership, share knowledge, challenge the status quo and treat colleagues and customers with honesty and respect. **We're modernising the platform behind our rapidly growing HCM product, Emply People. As our Lead Integration Developer, you'll define the technical direction for APIs and integrations while helping evolve the platform towards a cloud-native architecture.

As a senior team member, you will be involved in hands-on coding, design, development, customization, configuration, testing, and deployment of enterprise software solutions. Additionally, you will mentor and coach colleagues while making key technical decisions, combining hands-on development with technical leadership.

Emply People is a flexible HR solution for small and medium-sized businesses, supporting the full employee journey, from recruitment and onboarding to performance, time and absence management, and offboarding.

We're transitioning to modern technologies including microservices, containerisation and serverless architectures. You'll play a key role in this transformation from an integration perspective, helping build a more scalable, efficient and agile platform.

We're looking for a Lead Developer with strong hands-on experience building enterprise-grade integrations using the .NET stack.

**What You Will Do

**Besides your daily role in Emply, you'll be part of a team of seven Lead Developers across Paychex. You'll work closely with our Architect, Product Owner/Specialist, Scrum Master, and development teams in Poland and Ukraine to design, develop, and support our browser-based product within an agile Scrum framework.

**As Lead Integration Developer, You'll Be Responsible For

**

• Defining integration architecture in collaboration with the Architect.

• Owning integration patterns and standards.

• Designing scalable APIs and integration services.

• Improving technical implementations, simplifying the codebase, and promoting coding best practices.

• Improving reliability, performance, and observability.

• Guiding the migration towards cloud-native services.

• Mentoring developers and raising engineering standards.

**What Will Help You Succeed

**We encourage you to apply even if you don’t tick every single box. The following experience and skills will help you succeed in this role:

• 10+ years of proven experience designing and developing enterprise applications.

• Experience modernising legacy codebases and working with non-functional requirements such as security, performance, and scalability.

• Strong ownership of architecture and the ability to drive critical technical decisions.

• Hands-on experience with C#/.NET, MS SQL, Hangfire, REST, and GraphQL.

• Experience with API/interface modelling using OpenAPI.

• Strong understanding of integration, including enterprise integration patterns, synchronous vs. asynchronous integration, and related trade-offs.

• Experience with Domain-Driven Design (DDD).

• Experience with Git and development tools such as Azure DevOps and Jira.

• A proactive approach, with the ability to work independently and take ownership.

• Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts in clear business terms and act as a technical sparring partner and mentor to other developers.

• Excellent written and spoken English

**What We Offer

**In addition to Emply's incredible people and mission, we strive to foster a motivating and uplifting culture. Our offices are bright and open, with locations in Denmark and Germany. We work closely across teams and encourage a social culture, believing that working together socially makes tackling challenges more enjoyable. You will work in our Østerbro office, in a team that cares about its members and enjoys a good laugh. In short, you’ll experience plenty of learning and exciting challenges in a great work environment.

Emply is part of Paychex Europe, a leading provider of HCM solutions. Paychex Europe is growing rapidly and expanding into the European market, constantly seeking passionate talent to join them on this exciting journey. Find out more at www.emply.com.

We value different perspectives and believe diverse teams make better decisions. If this role interests you and you can see yourself contributing to our team, we encourage you to apply!

For questions about the role, please do not hesitate to contact Jacob Borella jborella@paychex.eu. Applications are reviewed continuously, and we look forward to meeting candidates who are excited about this opportunity.

Respect and partnership are at the heart of how we work together. We welcome applications from all qualified individuals, regardless of age, gender identity, ethnicity, sexual orientation, disability, religion or background. At Paychex Europe, we strive to create an inclusive environment where everyone can contribute and thrive. Our hiring decisions are based on skills, experience and potential.

Start date: As soon as possible

Full time, 40 hours per week.

**PAYCHEX EUROPE

**Paychex Europe delivers Payroll, HR, and Workforce Management solutions that simplify processes, save time, and provide insights that help businesses support their people and drive success. Built on over 50 years of expertise, our solutions adapt to changing needs — helping businesses run more efficiently, today and tomorrow.

jobs.description:
Join us in this role where you’ll be responsible of collecting and processing data from our energy assets at Skærbæk Power Station. We’re undertaking a digitalization and modernization effort to automate, improve, and standardize our data processing to ensure high data quality. In this role regular physical visits to our locations at Avedøre Power Station and in the Gentofte office should be expected.

**Welcome to Bioenergy

**You’ll be part of Data & Application where you, together with your colleagues, will be responsible of environmental and non-financial calculations for regulatory reporting, customer settlement and internal ESG reporting for Ørsted’s Danish combined heat and power plants. We have workplaces in Skærbæk, Gentofte, and at Avedøre Power Station, and we visit our energy assets on site when needed. Data & Application is part of Digitalisation & Technology, offering a collaborative environment with passionate and skilled colleagues. As a team, we in close dialogue with colleagues across the organization. We work hybrid: daily coordination on MS Teams and workplaces in Skærbæk, other sites, or from home as needed.

**You’ll play an important role in:

**

• being data responsible for Skærbæk Power Station — ensuring relevant data is available for reporting and settlement

• utilizing technical insight to ensure complete, correct & validated data

• monitoring and reporting CO₂ emissions, including validating data, maintaining traceable documentation, and ensuring compliance with applicable legislation

• managing flue gas emissions data and reporting, including follow-up on emission limits, permit conditions and regulatory documentation

• participating in process optimization incl. knowledge sharing across the team.

**To succeed in the role, you:

**

• possess a highly curious and analytical mindset, with a strong interest in process engineering and data reporting

This is not a software architecture role.

At Coloplast, we develop and manufacture physical medical devices used by millions of people worldwide. As a Senior System Architect, you will help define the architectural foundations of future product families and platforms, enabling innovation, scalability, and efficient product development across generations of products.

You will shape how platforms are structured to support reuse, new technology, portfolio growth, manufacturability, and long-term business value together with other R&D disciplines.

Working at the intersection of product development, manufacturing, quality, and systems engineering, you will balance user needs, product performance, regulatory requirements, risk, and platform strategy to create robust and scalable architectural solutions. Your work will ensure that future products are built on well-defined architectural foundations that enable both innovation and efficient execution.

Join a team shaping the future of R&D

You will become part of our Requirements Engineering Team within the Centre of Excellence in R&D.

The team consists of highly skilled specialists within Requirements Engineering and Systems Architecture, working with our processes and platforms.

We support development projects across the organization and continuously strengthen how systems development is conducted in a regulated medical device environment.

Design architecture that enable innovation

Working closely with product teams and stakeholders across R&D, you will transform business needs, user needs, stakeholder requirements, and technical opportunities into architecture decisions that balance innovation, manufacturability, regulatory compliance, risk, cost, and long-term scalability.

Specifically, you will:

Define and drive the platform strategy for a dedicated business area, enabling scalable product families, reusable platform assets, and accelerated delivery of future products.

• 
Drive architectural decomposition into system capabilities, subsystems, interfaces, and architectural building blocks.

Establish and maintain architecture documentation and system structures.

• 
Define system boundaries, interfaces, and allocation of functionality across the system.

Identify opportunities for platform reuse, standardization, modularization, and scalability.

Facilitate architectural trade-offs across business, technical, manufacturing, quality, regulatory, and user perspectives.

• 
Provide architectural guidance that ensures alignment between product architecture, platform strategy, manufacturing, quality, and development activities.

• 
Support the understanding of the systems architecture discipline and the synergies to other development disciplines through close collaboration with key stakeholders across R&D and beyond

Strong architecture experience within complex product development

You combine strong systems thinking with the ability to navigate complexity and create practical solutions.

• Experience defining system architecture and driving technical decisions in product development programs.

• Strong understanding of systems thinking and Systems Engineering principles.

• Experience working across multiple engineering disciplines.
